findings.title: Claim-less SQL callers are treated as trusted by social_guard_*
evidence: supabase/migrations/* social_guard_* functions branch on auth.uid()/claims
findings.impact: If a grant is ever widened, a claim-less caller (e.g. anon) could take the trusted branch; today the functions are service-role-only.
findings.recommendation: Make the trusted branch require an explicit service-role assertion rather than the absence of claims; add a negative test.

report: RLS deep dive: 43 CREATE POLICY statements, 106 SECURITY DEFINER functions, owner-scoped SELECT with service-role writes, and 16 SQL negative suites run in CI. Residual: some social_guard_* SQL paths treat a caller with no JWT claims as trusted (resolved earlier as SEC-P3-001), which is safe only while those functions remain service-role-only.
